open_points.subject: State 1 model inventory
open_points.text: === State 1: 01_models.md — the units under review ===
open_points.question: Which runtime models, value objects, entities, enums and read-only domain records represent the product facts named by State 0?
options: Declare separate models for connections, scanned files, placements, publication records and operation results
Use fewer aggregate models with nested values
Treat some named records and results as unmodelled dictionaries or primitives
open_points.default_guess: Declare explicit models for Connection, DeliverableFile, Placement, PublicationRecord and the three operation results.

open_points.subject: connection record
open_points.text: a connection record the owner has confirmed
open_points.question: What facts constitute a connection record, is it a value or entity, who mints its identity, and from which object, project, root, subfolder and confirmation facts?
options: An entity minted by the deliverer for one project/object and its confirmed folders
A value identified structurally by project and folder paths
An external entity minted by the agent or calling flow
open_points.default_guess: An entity minted by the deliverer from the project/object association and normalized folder bindings.

witness.initial: No connection exists for project P and object O.
events: The owner, through the agent, connects O's folders for P.
The calling flow later asks to scan P.
outcomes: The deliverer creates a durable Connection entity with its own identifier.
The deliverer treats the project-and-folder tuple as the connection's identity and creates no independent entity.
witness.observer: The calling flow and any persistence implementation

open_points.subject: object-to-project relationship
open_points.text: Connect an object to its folders (owner, through the agent)
open_points.question: How is the connected object related to the project used by scan and delivery, and is a connection identified or constrained per object, per project, or per object-project pair?
options: Exactly one object connection per project
Multiple objects may be connected to one project
One object may be shared by multiple projects through distinct connections
open_points.default_guess: Use one distinct connection entity per project-object pair.

open_points.subject: connection confirmation lifecycle
open_points.text: an unconfirmed connection delivers nothing
open_points.question: Is confirmation a mutable status of the same connection, a separate confirmation record, or a prerequisite that prevents a connection model from being created, and which product action performs the transition?
options: Create an unconfirmed Connection and later change it to confirmed
Create a separate confirmation record attached to a Connection
Create a Connection only after confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Create an unconfirmed Connection entity and let the owner's connect/confirm action transition it to confirmed.

witness.initial: The owner has supplied valid folder bindings but has not confirmed them.
events: The calling flow requests a scan.
The owner then confirms the binding.
The calling flow requests another scan.
outcomes: One Connection entity changes from unconfirmed to confirmed.
No Connection exists before confirmation; confirmation creates it.

open_points.subject: connection replacement and uniqueness
open_points.text: connects an object to its folder
open_points.question: If the owner connects the same object or project again with different folders, does the action mutate the existing connection, mint a new connection, or allow multiple active connections?
options: Update one connection entity in place
Create a replacement entity and retire the old one
Allow multiple simultaneous connection entities
open_points.default_guess: Update the single active project-object connection in place.

open_points.subject: deliverable file
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: What model represents each listed file, is it a value or entity, and is its identity based on project plus file name, source id, source content, or a particular observed file version?
options: An entity identified by project and source content
An entity identified by project and source id
A value snapshot identified structurally by file name, metadata and observed content
open_points.default_guess: An entity scoped to the project and identified by source content, with file name and current observation as facts.

events: Syncthing replaces a.jpg with different bytes.
The calling flow scans P again.
outcomes: The second scan describes a new deliverable identity because the content changed.
The second scan updates the existing deliverable because its project and file name are unchanged.

open_points.subject: source id
open_points.text: with its source id
open_points.question: Who mints the source id, from what facts, and is it the identity of a file observation, source content, placement request, or another model?
options: The deliverer derives it from source content
The deliverer derives it from project and file identity
The calling flow supplies and owns it
Syncthing or another upstream source supplies it
open_points.default_guess: The deliverer mints a project-scoped source id from the observed source content.

open_points.subject: source id flow
open_points.text: | Calling flow → deliverer | project id, file name, source id, Portal photo id | authenticated by the deliverer's own bearer token |
open_points.question: If scan reports a source id while the calling flow also sends a source id, is the sent value copied from the scan result, independently minted by the caller, or used only for a later operation, and which models carry it?
options: Scan mints and returns it; later deliver and record requests echo it
The caller mints it before scan or delivery
Scan and caller use different source-id concepts
open_points.default_guess: Scan returns a deliverer-minted source id that the caller must echo in later deliver and record-publication requests.

open_points.subject: status model
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Are ready, placed, published and rejected values of one closed status enum, variants of a status union with different facts, or projections derived from separate placement and publication models?
options: One enum plus optional source id and rejection reason fields
A discriminated union with status-specific required fields
A read projection derived from file, placement and publication entities
open_points.default_guess: Use a discriminated status union so rejected requires a reason and placed/published can require their associated facts.

open_points.subject: source id presence by status
open_points.text: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Does every ready, placed and published item have a source id, and does a rejected item have one as well as its reason?
options: Ready, placed and published have source ids; rejected does not
Every status, including rejected, has a source id
Only published has a source id
open_points.default_guess: Every observed file has a source id when content can be identified; rejection before identification has only file identity and reason.

open_points.subject: rejection
open_points.text: or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Is rejection a durable lifecycle status of a deliverable, a transient scan result, or an operation-result variant, and what later action can change or reread it?
options: A durable status that later scans may change
A transient status emitted independently by each scan
A failure result only, outside the file lifecycle
open_points.default_guess: Treat rejection as a transient scan or delivery result rather than a durable terminal state.

witness.initial: A file is rejected because its observed input is unusable.
events: The calling flow scans the project.
The owner replaces the file with usable bytes.
outcomes: The same deliverable entity transitions from rejected to ready.
The first rejection was only a scan result and the replacement produces a new observation.

open_points.subject: rejection reason
open_points.text: rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Is the rejection reason free text, a closed reason model, or a structured value, and is it part of the rejected status or a separate operation failure?
options: A closed enum of product reasons
A structured reason model with a code and safe detail
An unrestricted string
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed reason enum with an optional safe detail field.

open_points.subject: file metadata
open_points.text: file names, file metadata and bytes
open_points.question: Which file metadata facts enter a State 1 model, which model owns them, and are they merely an untrusted observation or part of file/source-content identity?
options: A FileObservation value carries only metadata needed by product rules
All available filesystem metadata is retained on the file model
Metadata is read transiently and no model records it
open_points.default_guess: Create a FileObservation value containing only the metadata needed to determine product facts, and exclude metadata from source-content identity.

open_points.subject: photo date
open_points.text: The photo date comes from the camera record, otherwise from the file's modification time, and is delivered as UTC without an offset.
open_points.question: Which model carries the photo date, does it also record whether the value came from the camera record or modification time, and at which action is that fact fixed?
options: Placement stores the date and its provenance when delivery occurs
The scanned file stores the date and provenance when scanned
Only the publication body carries the date, without provenance
open_points.default_guess: The scanned file carries date and provenance, and the placement snapshots both at delivery time.

open_points.subject: chosen source snapshot
open_points.text: a file whose content differs from the chosen one is not placed
open_points.question: What model records the chosen file version against which content is compared, who creates that identity evidence, and from which observation or source id?
options: The scan result contains a content identity echoed by delivery
The delivery request supplies an independently computed content identity
The deliverer remembers a server-side scan snapshot keyed by source id
open_points.default_guess: The scan result carries a deliverer-minted content identity that the delivery request echoes.

open_points.subject: source content
open_points.text: One placement exists per project and source content
open_points.question: What constitutes source-content identity at the model level, who mints it, and is it global or scoped to a project?
options: A deliverer-minted global content value derived from source bytes
A deliverer-minted identity scoped by project and bytes
The caller-provided source id is source-content identity
open_points.default_guess: Use a content-derived value minted by the deliverer, while placement uniqueness is scoped by project plus that value.

open_points.subject: placement
open_points.text: One placement exists per project and source content; repeating it changes nothing.
open_points.question: Is Placement an entity or value, who mints it, what facts it contains, and is its identity exactly project plus source content or a separate identifier constrained by that pair?
options: An entity with its own id and a uniqueness constraint on project plus source content
An entity whose composite identity is project plus source content
A pure value reconstructed from stored image facts
open_points.default_guess: A Placement entity whose composite identity is project plus source content.

open_points.subject: placement creation boundary
open_points.text: a prepared image in the Portal store, its reference and the publication body
open_points.question: Does successful delivery create the placement before, after, or atomically with the prepared binary and returned values, and which of those artifacts are facts of the Placement model?
options: Placement owns the stored-image reference and publication body and is created with them
The binary reference is a separate entity linked from Placement
Placement is only an idempotency record and the returned body is computed
open_points.default_guess: Create Placement with the stored-image reference and a snapshot of the publication body after the binary is successfully stored.

open_points.subject: failed delivery lifecycle
open_points.text: a photo that cannot be delivered is reported with its reason and no placement is made
open_points.question: Does failed delivery create or change any deliverable or failure model even though it creates no placement?
options: Return a transient failure value and persist nothing
Persist a rejected status on the deliverable
Create a durable delivery-attempt entity
open_points.default_guess: Return a transient failure value and create or change no persistent model.

witness.initial: A ready file has no placement.
events: The deliverer cannot prepare the photo.
outcomes: Only a failure result is returned; the file remains ready.
The file becomes durably rejected even though no placement is created.
witness.observer: The calling flow on its next scan

open_points.subject: stored file reference
open_points.text: its reference
open_points.question: What model represents the stored-file reference, who mints it, from what placement or binary-store fact, and how is it distinguished from the forbidden server path?
options: An opaque value minted by the deliverer from the stored object
An identifier minted by the Portal binary store
A field of Placement with no separate model
open_points.default_guess: Use an opaque value minted by the deliverer for the stored object and carried by Placement.

open_points.subject: publication body
open_points.text: the publication body
open_points.question: What product facts are in the publication-body model, is it a value snapshot or a view derived from Placement, and which action creates it?
options: An immutable value created and stored with Placement
A value derived whenever delivery is read
An opaque caller-specific dictionary
open_points.default_guess: An immutable typed value created with Placement from its stored-image reference and photo facts.

open_points.subject: delivery result
open_points.text: Deliver the same photo again | the first result, nothing written
open_points.question: What model is “the first result,” where is it retained or reconstructed, and does repeated delivery return the identical placement entity, an equal value result, or a fresh result object referring to the same placement?
options: Return the existing Placement with the same immutable result values
Reconstruct an equal DeliveryResult from Placement
Persist and return a separate first DeliveryResult entity
open_points.default_guess: Reconstruct an equal DeliveryResult value from the existing Placement.

open_points.subject: publication record
open_points.text: Record the publication | the file is reported as published, with its Portal photo id
open_points.question: Does recording publication mutate Placement, create a separate PublicationRecord entity, or only change a deliverable status, and who mints each identity?
options: Create a PublicationRecord identified by placement/source and Portal photo id
Mutate Placement from placed to published
Mutate only a file-status projection
open_points.default_guess: Create a PublicationRecord linked one-to-one to Placement; the Portal mints the Portal photo id and the deliverer mints or derives the record identity.

open_points.subject: Portal photo id
open_points.text: with its Portal photo id
open_points.question: Is the Portal photo id globally identifying, project-scoped, or meaningful only together with the placement/source, and is it stored as an opaque value or as an entity identity?
options: An opaque globally unique external id minted by the Portal
An opaque id scoped to a Portal project
Part of the PublicationRecord's composite identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an opaque external value minted by the Portal and constrain one value per placement.

open_points.subject: publication lifecycle
open_points.text: a photo that was not placed, or a different photo id for the same source, is refused and nothing is changed
open_points.question: What exact model transition changes placed to published, whether a repeated record with the same Portal photo id is idempotent, and whether publication can ever be replaced or removed?
options: Create publication once; the same id repeats idempotently and any different id is refused
Every repeat is refused, including the same id
The publication id may be replaced before the photo is shown
open_points.default_guess: Allow an idempotent repeat with the same Portal photo id and refuse a different id permanently.

witness.initial: Placement S has already been recorded with Portal photo id A.
events: The calling flow records publication again with A.
The calling flow later records publication with B.
outcomes: The repeat with A returns the existing publication and B is refused.
Both calls are refused because only the initial record action is valid.

open_points.subject: scan action model effects
open_points.text: scan a project's folder
open_points.question: Does scanning only return value snapshots, create or update durable file entities/statuses, or read placements and publications to derive statuses?
options: Pure read returning snapshots derived from folders plus placement/publication records
Upsert durable deliverable-file entities on every scan
Create immutable file-observation entities for every encountered version
open_points.default_guess: Treat scan as a read that returns value snapshots derived from the current folder observation and durable placement/publication records.

open_points.subject: status observability after source disappearance
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: If a source file is removed after placement or publication, does scan still report the placed/published model, omit it because there is no current file, or report another lifecycle status?
options: Continue reporting durable placed/published records
Report only files currently present and omit it
Report a rejected or unavailable item
open_points.default_guess: Continue reporting durable placed and published records even if the source file later disappears.

witness.initial: A source file is placed and recorded as published.
events: The calling flow scans the project.
outcomes: The published item remains visible from the durable publication record.
The item disappears because scan lists only current files.

open_points.subject: prepared image
open_points.text: A stored image carries no EXIF, GPS, XMP or comment, is upright and is at most 2000 px on its longest side.
open_points.question: Is the prepared image a distinct model from Placement and source content, and which of these accepted facts are stored model facts versus guarantees only of the binary artifact?
options: A PreparedImage value/entity records its reference and declared properties
Placement directly owns the reference and image facts
No runtime model represents the prepared image; only bytes embody the guarantees
open_points.default_guess: Use a PreparedImage value owned by Placement with the reference and relevant declared product facts.
